🇺🇸 A Tennessee trooper arrested former Wild Orchid singer Stefanie Fair for DUI, claiming her car SMELLED like alcohol 😳

Fair insisted she doesn’t drink. Video later showed she had visited an ice cream shop just 1 hour earlier.

Her blood test came back clean 2 months later, and the state is paying her $70,000, while the trooper faces no cost.

Tennessee has settled with at least 1 other sober driver, and hundreds of DUI cases in the state have ended with clean blood tests.

Writer: Lucas
 https://t.co/iL4UyOEGuM

🇺🇸 Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price in four days... and up to 303 million more insider shares unlock on December 15

Each of Anthropic's seven cofounders sold about $280 million worth at the IPO, which was disclosed up front, and veteran fund manager George Noble says that part doesn't bother him. The wave of early investor shares coming next does:

"The folks who participated in the IPO, they're just going to get run over."

Early backers bought in at a fraction of today's price, so every unlock date between now and February tests whether regular investors end up holding the bag.

@gnoble79

🇺🇸 Pentagon officials reportedly considered using a Cold War-era law to pressure Nvidia’s board into bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO 🤯

Pete Hegseth and deputy Steve Feinberg discussed using the Defense Production Act as leverage before announcing Huang’s return.

The law doesn’t clearly authorize the government to install a CEO, but one source said it could serve as a warning to shift more production toward military needs.

The Pentagon flatly denies the talks ever happened.

Nvidia’s board says it received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded Huang’s return posed no national security risk.

Source: Washington Post / Writer: Lucas

Finland's Immigration Service and National Bureau of Investigation screened approximately 20,000 people granted asylum or subsidiary protection, discovering that around 1,000 had serious criminal backgrounds.

The offenses included rape, child rape, aggravated assault, robbery, drug crimes, homicide and terrorism-related crimes. Three-quarters of those identified were Iraqi, Afghan or Syrian citizens.

Justice Minister Leena Meri called the figure "appalling" and demanded deportations, expressing hope that offenders would also receive permanent EU-wide entry bans.

Happy birthday to the legendary Tina Turner, who would’ve turned 87 today.

The 12x Grammy-winning icon is widely recognised as being the Queen of Rock ‘n’ Roll, making her mark as one of the best-selling music artists of all time. She made history in being the first Black artist and first woman to grace the cover of Rolling Stone magazine. During her career, she released major hits, such as ‘The Best’, ‘What’s Love Got to Do with It’, ‘We Don’t Need Another Hero’ and more.
